uk_vickers_gbt_155: After the multinational SP70 programme collapsed in the 1980s, VSEL designed the GBT 155: a 155 mm turret built around the FH-70 howitzer that could be fitted to Vickers Mk.3, Chieftain, Centurion or Challenger hulls as a cheap way to upgrade old tanks. It found no buyers, though the design fed into the AS90 and Poland's Krab. In the game it is quick for an artillery vehicle and its big gun reloads briskly, but the tall hull is easy to spot, the turret only keeps out rifle-calibre fire, and the packed ammunition often cooks off when penetrated. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
uk_vickers_mbt_mk_1: Vickers-Armstrongs built this export main battle tank as a private venture in the 1960s, combining the L7 105 mm gun, the Leyland L60 multi-fuel engine and Chieftain fire control and transmission into an affordable package. India adopted it as the licence-built Vijayanta, and Kuwait bought 70 adapted for desert use. In the game it suits a support or sniping role: gun depression is good and an aced crew reloads in five seconds, but the 4.9-6.0x sight limits long-range work, mobility is average and the flat turret front is weak, although the 60-degree hull plate gives moderate protection. It was added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
uk_vickers_mbt_mk_3: The last Vickers tank to win export orders, the Mk.3 reworked the Mk.1 with a cast turret front and mantlet, a Chieftain laser rangefinder in place of the ranging machine gun, and room for 50 rounds; Kenya and Nigeria ordered it in numbers and still field it. Compared with the Mk.1 it has a sturdier turret, 10 degrees of gun depression for hull-down play, a 720 hp engine that slightly improves mobility, and M456 HEAT-FS for targets that defeat APDS, though its sight is fixed at 10x. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
uk_vickers_mk7: A 1980s Vickers prototype, the Mk.7 put a turret with Chobham armour, a proven L11 120 mm gun and good fire control onto a Leopard 2 chassis, which makes it an unusual entry in the British tree. In the game that mix gives a rare balance: the German engine provides real mobility, the turret offers decent protection and the gun hits hard, backed by improved TOGS thermals, a laser rangefinder and smoke launchers. It suits several playstyles and was added in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
uk_vickers_mk_11: Vickers built the Mk.11 privately for an Australian long-range patrol vehicle tender, pairing a Timoney Mark 8 wheeled hull with the turret of the VFM5 light tank prototype; despite plans for APC, SPAA and other versions, only one prototype was made after work began in 1993. In the game it is big and thinly armoured, slow across rough ground but quick on roads, and it carries the familiar L7 gun with a laser rangefinder and can swim. It came with Update 2.31 "Kings of Battle".
uk_vickers_mk_6_aa_mk_1: Built after the fall of France to counter German air raids and dive bombers, this anti-aircraft conversion of the first Vickers Light Tank Mk.VI has a powered one-man turret with four 7.92 mm BESA machine guns. In the game it is extremely fragile, so concealment from both ground vehicles and aircraft matters. Low muzzle velocity and modest damage per hit mean holding fire until a plane is close and expecting to land many rounds, and several aircraft taking turns to strafe are a real danger. It was added in Update 1.79 "Project X".
uk_vijayanta: India's first home-built main battle tank was a licence-made Vickers Mk.1; a prototype reached India in 1964 and the type entered service the following year, fought in the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War, and some were still with border troops as late as 2019. The premium version in the game plays almost exactly like the Mk.1 but adds the M456 105 mm HEAT-FS round. Its armour is poor for its level, so it works best as a support tank kept well away from the front line. It arrived with the "La Royale" update.
uk_ystervark_spaa: South Africa's Ystervark ("porcupine") is a mine-protected anti-aircraft truck of the 1980s, made by taking one of the Project Sireb prototypes, the "Bulldog", and replacing its passenger compartment with a weapons mount. In the game its accurate, rapid-firing 20 mm GAI-C01 cannon brings down aircraft readily, but ammunition is limited, so short bursts are the rule. The crew sit fully exposed, making concealment vital, and HVAP rounds give some anti-tank ability that is best kept for emergencies. It came with the "Ground Breaking" update.
us_adats_bradley: ADATS is a modular dual-role missile system able to engage both aircraft and armoured vehicles; the US Army version sat on an M3 Bradley chassis with a 25 mm cannon and 12.7 mm machine gun added, but budget cuts, post-Cold War priorities and poor bad-weather performance killed it in the early 1990s before fielding. In the game its eight MIM-146 missiles double as anti-tank weapons, with up to 900 mm of penetration and a 6 kg TNT-equivalent warhead. Against aircraft, its 10 km reach can feel short. It was added in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
us_ags_teledyne: Teledyne Continental Motors' early-1980s entry for the Armored Gun System contest, meant to replace the M551 Sheridan, stood out for its unmanned turret; it lost to the CCVL and was later pitched for export. In the game the tiny turret is its great asset: from a good hull-down spot it is very hard to disable, helped by 10 degrees of gun depression. Anything with an autocannon or bigger can tear it apart once the hull is exposed, though, and lingering in one place invites artillery or bombs. It was a reward in the 2021 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. event, added in "Winged Lions".
us_ccvl: FMC's entry for the Armored Gun System competition to replace the M551 Sheridan used an autoloader to cut the crew to three; it was selected in 1992 and became the M8 AGS, though procurement was terminated in 1997. In the game it combines a soft-recoil, autoloaded 105 mm M68A1 gun with a two-plane stabiliser, laser rangefinder and gunner's thermal sight, plus excellent mobility. Its armour only stops heavy machine gun fire and shell fragments, so it is a fast, hard-hitting light tank rather than a brawler. It was a reward in the 2022 "Overpowered" event, added in "Drone Age".
us_efv_p1: General Dynamics developed the EFV from 1996 to 2011 to replace the US Marine Corps' AAV-7A1, adding a 30 mm Bushmaster and powerful water-jet propulsion, but changing doctrine and high costs led to its cancellation. In the game its huge hull is wrapped in layered composite screens on every side but the front, and the roomy interior lets it absorb hits that miss vital parts. On water it reaches 42 km/h, far quicker than other amphibians. The 30 mm cannon mainly threatens light vehicles or targets caught from the flank, which its bulk makes hard to arrange. It was a 2025 "Semper Fidelis" event reward in "Tusk Force".
us_halftrack_m13: White Motor Company produced the M13 MGMC, the first anti-aircraft version of the M3 half-track, from 1942 to 1943; it saw combat only at Anzio before the four-gun M16 replaced it in 1944. In the game its thin, upright armour offers almost nothing, so it relies on speed, handling and cover. The machine guns can hurt some light tanks, but aircraft should remain the priority, and artillery is a cue to move at once because fragments easily destroy it. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_halftrack_m15: One of the first vehicles in the American ground tree at Update 1.45 "Steel Generals", the M15 CGMC is an anti-aircraft half-track pairing a 37 mm cannon with Browning heavy machine guns. Compared with the machine-gun-only M13 and M16 it has real armour and a cannon that downs aircraft faster at range, but it carries far less ammunition, its mixed weapons are harder to aim, and the mount traverses slowly and cannot fire over the cab. The Brownings only fire on the machine gun key. It works best behind friendly lines with a clear view of the sky, ideally with the guns facing rearward.
us_halftrack_m16: The second anti-aircraft variant of the M3 half-track mounted four M2HB Brownings on an M45 quad mount; White built around 2,700 in 1943-44, and their deadliness against infantry and low-flying planes earned the nickname "Meat Chopper" before the type left US service in 1954. In the game it handles like the M13: too lightly armoured to fight tanks, but its guns set aircraft alight readily, provided it waits until they are near. Moving after each engagement helps it survive. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_halftrack_m3_75mm_gmc: Improvised for the new Tank Destroyer Branch after France fell in 1940, the M3 GMC simply placed a French-designed 75 mm gun on an M3 half-track; up to 2,200 were built from 1941 to 1943 and served in the Pacific, North Africa and Italy before the M10 took over. In the game the half-track body offers little survivability, but the gun hits hard for its rank and can deal with the odd medium or heavy tank at Rank I. The long reload is the catch, so every shot must count and a safe place to reload is essential. It came with Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_hstv_l: A late-1970s testbed from the joint Army and Marine Corps ARMVAL programme, the HSTV-L explored whether speed could replace heavy armour as protection; its centrepiece was the ARES XM274, a rapid-firing 75 mm hyper-velocity smoothbore meant to break composite armour with quick follow-up hits. Only one was built, and the Army settled on 105 mm as the minimum calibre for such vehicles. In the game it is a quick, hard-hitting flanker with a stabiliser, laser rangefinder, thermals and an autoloader cycling in as little as 1.5 seconds, plus excellent gun depression, though the small calibre can struggle against some MBTs head-on. It arrived in "Starfighters".
us_lav_ad: Built so the US Marine Corps' fast LAV battalions would have their own short-range air cover, the LAV-AD combined the LAV-25 hull with a rotary cannon plus Stingers; trials began in 1992 and 17 had been delivered by 1997. In the game it has virtually no armour, as even heavy machine guns go through the sides. Stingers work best against aircraft inside about 3 km, often forcing evasion even when they miss, while the gun covers targets too close for the missiles to arm. Swapping the Stingers for rocket pods, alongside HVAP rounds, lets it tackle light vehicles. It arrived in "Wind of Change".
us_losat_ccv: Lockheed Martin's MGM-166 LOSAT destroyed armour by impact energy alone, using an 80 kg missile flying at over Mach 4 that crossed its 4 km range in under four seconds; it was dropped in 2004 over slow reloads, cost, poor close-range results and little use against light targets. In the game it must see its target directly, which exposes it when firing, and the missiles are weak up close but defeat almost anything once at full speed. Lacking gun elevation or depression, it suits big, open maps where its speed can claim long sightlines; its armour is thin. It was a 2023 Tokushu Heiki event reward in "Sons of Attila".
us_lvt_4_zis_2: After capturing many LVT(A)(4) amphibians from the Nationalists in 1949 and losing access to American ammunition, China's People's Liberation Army replaced their 75 mm howitzer turrets with the high-velocity Soviet 57 mm ZiS-2 anti-tank gun. In the game this mix of American hull and Soviet gun can engage from much farther away than the standard LVT(A)(4), and despite light armour it is a serious opponent for vehicles of similar rank. Its tall shape and open-topped turret leave it very exposed to strafing aircraft and artillery. It was a 2016 "Winter Holiday" event reward in Update 1.65, later sold as a Warbonds trophy in April 2019.
us_lvt_a1_m24: In 1944 the US military proposed fitting the LVT(A)(1) with an M24 turret and its 75 mm gun, but the widened turret ring made the vehicle unstable when firing afloat; a redesign was planned when Japan's surrender ended the programme, and the lessons fed into a 76 mm version. In the game it swaps the regular LVT(A)(1)'s 37 mm for a 75 mm whose APCBC rounds do far more damage after penetrating, and it gains a heavy machine gun. The cost is a larger silhouette, unchanged armour and a slower reload. It came with Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
us_lvt_a_1: Pacific landings showed the Marines needed more than heavy machine guns for fire support, so the LVT amphibian family gained the LVT(A)(1), with an M3-style turret carrying a 37 mm gun stabilised to shoot while afloat and extra machine guns on the rear deck; 509 were built. In the game it is an entry-level light tank with firepower close to the M3 light tank and the rare ability to cross water. The thin plating needed for buoyancy stops little beyond rifle-calibre fire, but it gives newcomers a distinctly different way to play. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
us_lvt_a_1_trb: An FMC amphibious tank derived from the LVT-2, the LVT(A)(1) carried a lightly modified M3 Stuart turret; 510 were built between December 1943 and late 1944 for US Army and Marine assaults on Japanese-held islands. This version, with its own camouflage, was given out in 2023 to players who used TheRussianBadger's partner link. In the game its gun reloads quickly and penetrates respectably, but armour is limited and the huge hull is hard to hide; even so, it adapts well to both aggressive and cautious play.
us_lvt_a_4: When Marines judged the LVT(A)(1)'s 37 mm too weak, the LVT(A)(4) took a modified turret from the M8 Scott howitzer carriage, adding a roof-mounted 12.7 mm Browning and dropping the rear-deck machine guns; 1,890 were built, most for the US Army and 50 for Britain. In the game this premium beginner light tank matches the M8's firepower while being able to swim, though its thin hull stops little beyond rifle-calibre fire. The slow shells can arc over low cover onto light vehicles, and the Browning handles light vehicles and slow, low aircraft well. It was a 2020 Victory Day reward in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
us_m10: Rushed out for the Tank Destroyer Branch formed after the fall of France, the M10 GMC put a high-velocity 3-inch gun in a large open-topped turret on an M4A2 Sherman hull and served from Tunisia to the end of the Second World War; the "Wolverine" name is probably post-war. In the game it shares the Sherman's drivetrain with a more sloped hull, and the 3-inch gun, which has no muzzle brake unlike later 76 mm weapons, penetrates most enemies it lines up on. Slow turret traverse is the big weakness, making it hard to react to surprise threats. It came with Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_m103: Alarmed by the IS-3's debut at the 1945 Berlin parade, the US began the T43 heavy tank in 1948 and rushed it into production during the Korean War, which led to lengthy rebuilds; 300 were standardised as the M103, mostly for the Marine Corps, and served until 1974. In the game everything centres on its huge 120 mm gun, whose HEAT rounds can deal with anything it meets. The armour is a bonus rather than a shield, since HEAT and APDS defeat the front fairly easily, though the rounded, uneven shapes cause some ricochets. It is slow and lags behind most allies. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m109a1: Entering US service in 1973, the M109A1 upgraded the M109 howitzer with the longer 155 mm M185 gun, stretching range from 14.6 km to 18 km; it backed US forces in Europe and the Middle East, and survivors were later converted to M109A2 standard. In the game it resembles the Soviet 2S3M, lobbing heavy 155 mm shells a long way with a poor rate of fire but plenty of ammunition. Good speed and acceleration let it relocate and avoid direct fights, which matters because its armour is thin, and low gun depression rules out shooting down from high ground. It arrived in "Kings of Battle".
us_m10_booker_late: Named after two decorated soldiers, the M10 Booker came from the US Army's Mobile Protected Firepower programme, launched in 2015 to give infantry brigades a direct-fire vehicle they had lacked since the Sheridan's retirement; General Dynamics' Griffin II, on the ASCOD 2 chassis, won in 2022, but the Army cancelled it in April 2025 after only 26 had been built. In the game it is a sensor-rich light tank whose thermal sights and an IRST able to follow low-flying aircraft make it a strong scout, backed by a 105 mm gun to exploit what it finds. It was added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
us_m1128_mgs: The Mobile Gun System member of the Stryker family was developed by General Dynamics Land Systems for the US Army's Interim Armored Vehicle programme; 142 were built from 2002, but maintenance costs and weaker protection than other Strykers led to retirement by 2021. In the game it is a fast wheeled vehicle with a 105 mm gun and M900 ammunition, putting its firepower near the IPM1. Anything above autocannon calibre goes through its armour, even with the optional slat kit, so scoot-and-shoot is the way to play. Only 5 degrees of gun depression and a tall profile make safe firing spots harder to find. It arrived in "New Power".
us_m1128_wolfpack: Derived from Canada's LAV III Kodiak and in US Army service from 2006, the M1128 Stryker wheeled assault gun has steel hull armour backed by ceramic plates, rated against 14.5 mm fire, and can take slat screens against RPGs and missiles. Its name honours two posthumous Medal of Honor recipients, Stuart and Robert Stryker. The Wolfpack differs from the regular M1128 only in lacking hull slat screens and wearing a forest camouflage, so it keeps the same quick handling, light armour and capable armament. It was added in Update 2.23 "Apex Predators".
us_m1296_dragoon: The Dragoon came from a 2015 effort to up-gun the M1126 Stryker for the 2nd Cavalry Regiment in Germany, adding a remotely operated 30 mm turret to fill the gap between the machine-gun Stryker and the 105 mm MGS; 81 were converted, entering service from December 2017. In the game it shares the Stryker's excellent mobility, suiting both point capture and surprise flanks, and its fast-firing Bushmaster II has an APFSDS belt. It is large and lightly armoured, has only two crew and carries no ATGMs for heavier targets. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
us_m163_vulcan: Early in the Vietnam War the 40 mm Bofors of the M42 Duster could not fire fast enough against jets, so the US adapted the 20 mm Vulcan rotary cannon from its own aircraft as the M168 and mounted it with a tracking radar on an M113 chassis; Stinger-armed systems such as the Avenger eventually replaced it. In the game its huge rate of fire is the main asset, though range and overall capability fall short of the Gepard, Marksman or ZSU-23-4. That pushes it fairly close to the front, where it must take care not to be spotted by tanks. It was added in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
us_m18_hellcat: Buick's T70 was the fast, 76 mm-armed tank destroyer the US Tank Destroyer Branch had wanted since the fall of France; it was ordered into production as the M18 GMC in summer 1943, nicknamed "Hellcat" by its builder, and fought in battles such as the Bulge. In the game it is extremely fast and agile, with a strong gun in a fully rotating turret that gives a wider field of fire than casemate destroyers, at the cost of a taller profile. Its armour is only 12.7 mm, so almost anything gets through, though AP shells sometimes pass straight out the other side. Added in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it was reclassed as a light tank in May 2021.
us_m18_hellcat_black_cat: A gift twin of the regular M18 Hellcat, the "Black Cat" differs very little in performance. Sold in a pack from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it left the store after the sixth anniversary sale and returned for the seventh as a Golden Eagle purchase. APCR shells for its 76 mm gun give it an answer to common opponents such as the Panther D, Tiger H1 and IS-1. The fully rotating turret allows a wider arc of fire than casemate destroyers like the StuG III, at the price of a slightly taller shape, and high agility makes flanking its strength.
us_m18_hellcat_kit_3rank: This Hellcat represents the M18s that served with tank destroyer battalions of Patton's 4th Armored Division, fighting at Arracourt in September 1944 and at Noville near Bastogne, where four from the 705th helped paratroopers against the 2nd Panzer Division. Compared with the tech-tree M18 it adds extra armour, a camouflage net, an identification plate fitted so Allied troops would not mistake it for a German tank, and a 7.62 mm Browning. In play it is the familiar fast flanker with a strong 76 mm gun and APCBC shells, held back by thin armour and an open turret roof. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
us_m18_super_hellcat: To spread 90 mm firepower as widely as possible once the M36 arrived, US designers simply set an M36 turret on the nimble M18 hull; the result, called the "Super Hellcat", worked, but the war ended before it could be produced. In the game it pairs the M36's firepower with the M18's mobility, so the 90 mm defeats armour the 76 mm cannot. The M82 shell is the highlight: fired into flanks, which its speed helps it reach, its strong post-penetration damage can often knock out a tank with one hit. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
us_m19: Twin 40 mm Bofors on an M24 Chaffee chassis made the M19 MGMC, completed at the end of 1944 but not operational until after the war; its first combat came in Korea in 1950. The M19A1 adds a small auxiliary engine-generator so the guns work with the main engine off, plus stowage for two spare barrels. In the game it is versatile: AP and HE belts let the Bofors hurt light vehicles as well as aircraft, and its agility allows early flanking. Most of the crew sit in the open, though, with ammunition stored around the turret. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m1_abrams: After the MBT-70 and XM803 were cancelled, Chrysler's design beat General Motors for the XM1 contract in November 1976 and was accepted in 1981 as the M1 Abrams; 2,374 were built, and the type was upgraded repeatedly, eventually with a 120 mm gun. In the game it opens the American Abrams line, its turbine giving great speed and acceleration for repositioning and hit-and-run play. The armour is a clear step up, solid against kinetic rounds and especially strong against HEAT. It keeps the late M60's 105 mm gun and ammunition, but its mobility helps it reach enemy weak spots. It came with Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
us_m1_abrams_kvt: A premium gift tank from the "La Royale" update, the M1 KVT is an Abrams disguised with Soviet-style features. Unlike the real vehicle, which was converted from an M1A1, the in-game version is based on the original M1. Its disguise includes a rubber-fabric front screen in place of the side skirts, a netted barrel, a dummy IR searchlight, mock ERA blocks on the turret and glacis, two external fuel drums at the rear and turret boards reading "ЛОДКА" ("boat"), while the loader's M240 has been removed.
us_m1_ip_abrams: The Improved Performance M1 brought the stronger turret armour developed for the 120 mm M1E1 to the 105 mm Abrams, along with a turret bustle rack and trimmed rear skirts; 894 were built from 1984 to 1986, and it took part in the 1987 Canadian Army Trophy and Desert Shield without seeing combat. In the game the thicker composite in the turret cheeks resists both kinetic and HEAT rounds better than on the M1, encouraging more aggressive play, and the M900 APFSDS round penetrates more easily. The hull is unchanged, and the big turret ring remains vulnerable. It was added in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
us_m1a1_abrams: Fitted with the 120 mm M256 smoothbore after trials on the M1E1, the M1A1 was accepted in 1984 and built from 1985 to 1993; counting rebuilt M1s and IPM1s, around 5,000 exist, and it fought in Desert Storm and Iraqi Freedom. In the game it gives the fast Abrams the 120 mm gun, with only APFSDS and HEAT-FS available, and better-protected enemies may still need shots on weak points. Its composite armour holds well against HEAT and against kinetic rounds from weaker opponents, but mobility is the defence against stronger ones. Blow-out panels over the bustle ammunition help stop a cook-off from destroying it. It came with Update 1.87 "Locked On".
us_m1a1_abrams_yt_cup_2019: Awarded to the teams that won the 2019 YouTube Cup, this M1A1 arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy"; only its unique camouflage sets it apart from the standard tank. Historically, the M1A1 gave the Abrams the 120 mm M256 smoothbore, entering service in 1984 with around 5,000 eventually built or converted, and it saw combat in Desert Storm and Iraqi Freedom. In play it keeps everything the regular M1A1 offers: it survives hits well, moves superbly and carries potent ammunition, which puts it among the best main battle tanks in its bracket.
us_m1a1_aim_abrams: Australia bought 59 refurbished M1A1 AIM tanks from the US to replace a Centurion and Leopard fleet judged unable to protect crews against modern threats; the AIM ("Abrams Integrated Management") rebuild adds sensors and communications, and the tanks entered Australian service in 2007. In the game it keeps most of the M1A1's strengths with upgraded armour and fire control on top. Its KE-W APFSDS penetrates less than the M1A1's M829A1 but still threatens most opponents it will meet. It was added in "Danger Zone" as a squadron unlock.
us_m1a1_hc_abrams: Developed after the US Marine Corps chose the Abrams to replace its M60A1s, this M1A1 variant with Marine-requested changes went into production in November 1990 and served both services; the Army called it the M1A1 HC ("Heavy Common"), the Marines simply the "Common". In the game it adds the Heavy Armor upgrade with depleted uranium inserts and gains the M830A1 HEAT-FS round, whose proximity fuse lets it threaten low-flying aircraft too. Mobility is much as before, so it is essentially a stronger M1A1. It came with the "Direct Hit" update.
us_m1a1_hc_usmc: Click-Bait is a real Marine Corps M1A1 HC that became an internet curiosity after a photo showed it on deployment with a plastic garden chair on its roof; like other Marine HCs it carries the AN/VLQ-8A soft-kill protection system, a feature not found on other main-line Abrams. The premium version reproduces the chair and the kill markings on its barrel and otherwise matches the tech-tree M1A1 HC. Its mobility gets it to good positions quickly, and a quick reload lets it finish off targets that survive the first shot. It arrived in "Air Superiority".
